title: On the Mystery of Holy Matrimony; On the Duties of Husbands and Wives in Marriage
attribution_note: St Tikhon of Zadonsk (1724–1783). Two chapters, on the mystery of marriage and on the duties of husbands and wives. Translated here fresh from the Russian for this edition. Sources: https://www.ccel.org/contrib/ru/Tikhon1/Tikh101.html and https://predanie.ru/book/218962-o-lichnyh-obyazannostyah-kazhdogo-hristianina/?chapter=chapter_75

pairs.en:
On the mystery of holy matrimony
Q. What is marriage?
A. Marriage is a mystery through which a man and a woman, with the mutual consent of both, through the blessing of the priest, are united.
Q. What is the matter or substance of marriage?
A. A man and a woman.
Q. What is the form or completion?
A. The consent of both to take each other in marriage, and to keep love between them, so that neither shall leave the other until the end of their life.
Q. What must be kept in this mystery?
A. Three things. 1. Those wishing to enter marriage should prepare themselves with pious deeds, confess their sins, and partake of the Divine mysteries, three or four days before the wedding. 2. They should have a right intention, so that they may be united not like beasts, and not for the sake of fleshly pleasure, but so that the human race may be multiplied to the glory of God, through blessed birth and God-pleasing child-rearing. 3. There should be no impediment, such as kinship between them, fleshly or spiritual; likewise a forbidden time, such as fasting, or violence from parents unwilling to give their children in marriage, and other similar things.

sections.heading: The duties of husbands and wives

pairs.en:
On the duties of husbands and wives in marriage
First. Both husband and wife must enter marriage of their own free will and consent, therefore the priest at the wedding asks both persons: do you enter marriage of your own will and with consent? Therefore marriage without the consent of both persons cannot be firm; and priests, seeing the unwillingness of any person and yet performing the wedding, sin gravely and are subject to proper punishment, because from this all evil in marriage follows.
Second. Those who have properly entered marriage must keep love and faithfulness to each other until the end of life.
Third. Neither husband nor wife should leave each other until death, but, as they promised and agreed, remain inseparable until the end.
Fourth. Husband and wife should consider virtue, not passion, as the foundation of their love, that is, when the husband sees some fault in his wife, he should gently instruct her and the wife should obey her husband in this. Likewise the wife, when she sees some fault in her husband, should admonish him and he is obliged to listen to her. Thus their love will be faithful and continuous, and they, having made their happiness through this, will be gladdened by the virtue and well-being of their children, and the blessing of God will be upon them. There is a custom for some husbands to leave their wives and wives to leave their husbands, under the pretense of abstinence, but this is very dangerous: because instead of abstinence the grave sin of adultery may follow, either for one or for both. If the husband leaves the wife, and the wife sins with another, then the husband is guilty of this sin, because he gave his wife the occasion to sin. Likewise the wife, if she leaves her husband, and the husband sins with another, then the wife is guilty of this sin for the reason described above.
Fifth. The Apostle says to those in marriage: "The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband; likewise the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife. Do not deprive each other, except by agreement, for a time, for the purpose of fasting and prayer" [1 Cor. 7:4-5] and so on. It is clear what the Apostle is speaking about here.
Sixth. Those living in marriage should remember that they are Christians, confess the holy name of God, call upon God and pray, partake of the Holy Mysteries of Christ, and so on, and even more so priests and deacons. And therefore they should not live in marriage like pagans, as the Apostle says to them: "That Satan may not tempt you through your incontinence" [1 Cor. 7:5].
Seventh. The husband should not treat his wife as a slave, but as a helper; but the wife should obey her husband, as the Apostle teaches: "Wives, submit to your husbands as to the Lord." And a little further: "Let the wife fear her husband" [Eph. 5:22, 33]. And in another place: "Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord" [Col. 3:18]. When husband and wife are of one mind and virtuous, then marriage will be prosperous and beautiful, because they will always have unity of mind, agreement, and peace, in which consists great prosperity. "Behold what is good, or what is beautiful, but for brethren to dwell together" [Ps. 132:1], says the Prophet. But since Satan, the enemy of human souls, seeks to tear apart the bond of love and agreement among the virtuous, husband and wife should be lenient with each other in their weaknesses and bear with each other with love; and thus agreement and peace will be preserved.
